record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: How can a nearest-neighbor decision rule be made invariant to scaling of the measurements?

evidence.quote: How can the rule be made invariant to scaling of the measurements?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a feature space and let $T = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ with $x_i \in \mathcal{X}$ and $y_i$ a class label be a labeled training set. For a metric $\rho : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, the (1-)nearest-neighbor decision rule is the classifier
$$ f_{T,\rho}(x) \;=\; y_{i^*(x)}, \qquad i^*(x) \in \arg\min_{1 \leq i \leq n} \rho(x, x_i). $$
For any vector $s = (s_1, \dots, s_d) \in (0,\infty)^d$ of positive scale factors, let $D_s : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ denote the diagonal scaling $D_s(x) = (s_1 x_1, \dots, s_d x_d)$, and write $D_s(T) = \{(D_s(x_i), y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$.

Construct, in a fully data-driven way, a decision rule $g_T : \mathbb{R}^d \to \{\text{labels}\}$ depending only on the training set $T$, such that for every training set $T$, every query point $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and every $s \in (0,\infty)^d$,
$$ g_{D_s(T)}(D_s(x)) \;=\; g_T(x), $$
while $g_T$ retains the nearest-neighbor character (i.e., $g_T(x) = y_{i^*(x)}$ for some training index $i^*(x)$ chosen according to a notion of proximity that is intrinsically determined by $T$). In other words, design a nearest-neighbor classifier whose output is invariant under arbitrary coordinatewise rescalings of the measurements, and specify the proximity / metric construction that achieves this invariance.
artifact.status_search_result: Numerous approaches address scale sensitivity of nearest-neighbor classifiers, including feature standardization, Mahalanobis-distance learning, large-margin nearest-neighbor metric learning, and adaptive/dynamic feature-scaling schemes. These provide partial practical answers but there is no canonical fully-data-driven solution that is provably invariant under arbitrary coordinatewise rescalings while preserving nearest-neighbor semantics; the broader question is typically posed as an ongoing design challenge rather than a closed theorem, so the status is best described as unknown / informally open.

status_evidence.title: An Invariant Large Margin Nearest Neighbour Classifier
status_evidence.snippet: Extends LMNN to incorporate invariance to multivariate polynomial transformations approximating rotations and affinities.
status_evidence.claim: Metric-learning approaches partially address invariance for k-NN.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Feature Scaling for K-Nearest Neighbor Algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes dynamic feature scaling to mitigate the dependence of k-NN on feature scales.
status_evidence.claim: Feature-scaling heuristics are an active and partial response to the scale-sensitivity problem.

status_evidence.title: k-nearest neighbors algorithm - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Accuracy of k-NN can be severely degraded by inconsistent feature scaling; research focuses on selecting or scaling features.
status_evidence.claim: No canonical fully scale-invariant nearest-neighbor rule is established as standard.
